title: SLI tiling and trace-context cookbook
content:
TL;DR:
Keep SLI tiles narrow and orthogonal (latency quantiles, success ratio, kv-warmth, token-cost). Use trace anchors (session_id, request_id, tenant_id, model_variant) to link tiles to a small set of representative traces. Prefer severity-weighted reservoir sampling for traces (so high-latency/errored requests are over-sampled), but cap by tenant to avoid noisy tenants dominating.

Why this doc exists:
- There are lots of dashboards showing similar numbers; operators still waste time recreating context when investigating a bad rollout.
- Goal: a compact cookbook for teams to construct tiled SLI dashboards that immediately point to a small set of traces with enough context to start RCA.
- Target audience: SREs + oncall, platform engineers owning rollouts, and solutions engineers doing customer postmortems.

Guiding principles (short):
- Single-responsibility tiles: each tile answers one question (e.g., "are user-visible latencies increasing?").
- Cross-link anchors: every tile must emit 2–3 trace attributes that join to traces/requests.
- Cost-visible panels: show token cost or GPU-seconds on the same cadence as latency.
- Tiled rollups: allow both tenant-level and global rollups without metric re-instrumentation.

Core metric definitions (recommended canonical names + units + tags):
- inference.request.count: count, tags=[tenant_id, model, region, route]
- inference.request.success_ratio: ratio (0..1), tags same as above, window=5m
- inference.latency.api_p50 / api_p95 / api_p99: ms, tags=[tenant_id, model_variant, region, route], compute at the raw-requests level then roll up
- tokens.generated.rate: tokens/sec, tags=[tenant_id, model]
- token.e2e.cost_per_request_usd: USD/request, tags=[tenant_id, model_variant]
- kvcache.warmth_ratio: ratio of requests served from prefix/KV vs cold, tags=[tenant_id, model_variant]
- model.fallback_rate: ratio, tags=[tenant_id, model_variant, fallback_reason]
- queue.backpressure: gauge of queue length / capacity, tags=[pool_id, hw_tier]

Rollup rules and why they matter:
- Percentiles must be computed from histograms at the service boundary; do not compute p95 from p50 of shards. Each process should export a histogram (exponential) with consistent buckets and a shard_id tag. Aggregation service computes global quantiles.
- For tenants with low QPS (<1 r/s), prefer sample-by-raw-requests + expose p50/p95 computed at tenant bucket level; for extremely low tenants show raw request list.
- When rolling up across regions, keep region tag and expose a region-broken heatmap tile rather than flattening.

Trace anchoring conventions (span attributes to encourage):
- span.attr.request_id = <uuid>
- span.attr.session_id = <hashed-session> (if present)
- span.attr.tenant_id = <tenant-id>
- span.attr.model_variant = e.g. "gptx-7b-q4f-2026"
- span.attr.kv_cache_hit = true|false
- span.attr.kv_prefix_length = int
- span.attr.kv_lookup_latency_ms
- span.attr.trigger = [api|dedicated|private]
- Important: emit token counts and GPU-bound times as attributes on the terminal span so we can filter slow traces by their GPU cost.

Sampling strategy (practical):
- Reservoir per-tenancy + severity weighting: keep a fixed-size reservoir per tenant per 1h window; weight on latency percentile bucket + error flag. This avoids a single noisy tenant drowning out others.
- Severity tiers: error > p99 > p95 > p50 > normal. Targets: errors 50% of sample, p99 30%, p95 15%, others 5% (tunable).
- Cost-aware cap: if a tenant exceeds cost threshold (e.g., >$1000/day), only sample top N problematic traces to keep storage manageable.

Dashboard layout recommendations (rows/tiles):
Row 1 - Global health snapshot (single line): total QPS, global success_ratio, global token_cost_last_1h, active_model_variants_count.
Row 2 - Latency slices (heatmap): latency buckets heatmap by region x model_variant (columns=percentile buckets). Click-to-filter should pre-populate trace query with region/model_variant attributes.
Row 3 - Tenant-level quick tiles: top-10 tenants by QPS. Each tile = small panel with p95, error rate, token_cost/h. Clicking tenant tile loads a tenant-scoped dashboard with trace links.
Row 4 - KV cache and cold-start signals: kvcache.warmth_ratio over time, prefix-hit distribution, median prefix_length; annotate with rollout events.
Row 5 - Cost & efficiency: tokens.generated.rate, token.e2e.cost_per_request_usd, GPU-seconds per 1k tokens.
Row 6 - Investigations: sample trace list generated by sampling strategy; each trace row shows request_id, p99 contribution, GPU-time, model_variant, tenant_id and a link to trace UI.

Alerting & SLOs (suggested baselines, adjust per product):
- SLO: success_ratio >= 99.9% over 30d for core hosted routes; alert if 30d burn rate > 2x expected.
- Latency SLO: p95(api latency) < 300ms for short prompts; p95 < 800ms for long-sequence prompts (separate SLOs).
- Warmth SLO: kvcache.warmth_ratio >= 0.85 for production tenant cohort; alert if sudden drop >10% vs 1h baseline.
- Cost SLO (ops guardrail): GPU-seconds per 1k tokens should not increase >20% post-rollout.

Investigation playbook (operator flow):
1) See global tile alert -> click into latency heatmap.
2) Use model_variant x region filter to identify impacted slice.
3) Open sample traces for that slice (severity-weighted); inspect terminal span attributes: token counts, GPU-time, kvcache flags.
4) If traces show kvcache misses with prefix_length=1 and high lookup latency, mark rollout as possible culprit.

Query examples (prometheus-like pseudo):
- p95: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(inference_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, model_variant, region))
- kvwarmth: sum(inference_kvcache_hits_total) / sum(inference_requests_total) by (tenant_id, model_variant)
- token-cost: sum(token_e2e_cost_usd_total) by (tenant_id) / sum(inference_requests_total) by (tenant_id)

Open questions / tradeoffs we still need decisions on:
- Should we standardize on one histogram bucket schema across all services or accept per-language libs with translation layer? (pros for standardization: accurate percentile rollups; cons: rollout burden)
- How strict should tenant caps be on trace retention in Dedicated customers with heavy usage? Legal/compliance may require longer retention for some enterprises.

Short TODOs (owners):
- Priya: prototype reservoir sampler in obs-playground (ticket OBS-1021) - due 2026-03-31.
- Ava: draft tenant-scoped dashboard template + JSON export that enforces trace anchors - due 2026-03-20.
- Diego: cost-overlay panel prototype and GPU-time attribute standard (PR #432) - in progress.
- Ruth: write operator runbook blurb for kvcache warm-start investigation - due 2026-03-18.

Notes to self / raw thoughts:
- Might be worth shipping a minimal "trace anchor SDK" that ensures every service emits the few attributes we rely on; even a tiny wrapper saves 15 min per incident.
- For private deployments, provide a knob to disable cross-tenant reservoir (we should be explicit about privacy boundaries).

References / links:
- OBS-987 (sampling design epic)
- GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/432
- Confluence draft: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/OBS/SLI+Tiling+Notes

End of notes.
